Net price a patient-year = the Part B figure over 1.06: $116,413 in 2025 ($123,397.49) and $114,344 in 2024 ($121,204.42, drug_demand). Stock = revenue over net price: 5,214 in 2025 and 4,712 in 2024. Starts in 2025 = 5,214 - 4,712 x (1 - 0.7724) = 4,142. Over the 12,450 patients a year entering the line (21,010 x 0.5926) that is 33.26%. MULTIPLE 0.2, A JUDGEMENT: 0.2 x 33.26% = 6.65%. It is half the 0.4 the mocertatug rezetecan row takes, the claimant nearest in timing, because mocertatug has a registered Phase 3 (NCT07286266, primary completion 2029-12-17) and published Phase 1 responses, and IMGN151 has neither
column12: the 0.2 multiple is a judgement and the figure the value rests on. The case for more: IMGN151 is designed for low and medium FRalpha tumours (in vivo regressions at H-scores of 30 to 140, AACR 2020 abstract 2890), which Elahere's label, set by MIRASOL at 75% or more of cells staining 2+ or above, leaves out, and AbbVie already sells Elahere to the same prescribers. The case against: no human efficacy has been disclosed since NCT05527184 started in January 2023; the Phase 1b confines its platinum-resistant monotherapy arms to China and Japan and runs its other arms in platinum-sensitive disease, so a US platinum-resistant label is not plainly the route AbbVie is taking, although the Phase 2 readout it names is in platinum-resistant disease; it would arrive about 2033 behind Rina-S (RAINFOL-02, NCT06619236, primary completion 2027-02), R-DXd, AZD5335, sofetabart mipitecan (FRAmework-01, NCT07213804, 2028-11) and mocertatug rezetecan; and AbbVie holds a third FRalpha ADC, ABBV-901, in Phase 1 in ovarian cancer (book asset 1680)

column11: derived and found to be nil: AbbVie generated $17,816mm of free cash flow on $61,160mm of revenue in FY2025, a 29.13% margin, against the 28.95% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The two reconcile to within a fifth of a point, which is why this is zero rather than absent: the check was run and it found nothing to charge. Restated before interest: ABBV paid $3,002mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2025, 4.91% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Restated at replacement capex: ABBV spent $1,214mm on plant over 2025 against $762mm of plant depreciation, 0.74% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge stays nil. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 32.46% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2025 supports 38.40%, so the charge rebuilds at -5.94%. It was held at nil, but ABBV books $7,377mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0001551152-26-000008), 12.06% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -5.94%. Restated without working capital build: over 2025 ABBV's cash flow statement shows receivables up $1,490mm, inventories up $234mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $951mm, a working capital build of $773mm, 1.26% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -5.94% to -7.35%.

The older windows would imply a credit, not a cost: 33.6% over three years and 36.3% over five, both above the model, because they carry peak Humira.
